title: The kernel of any surjection from a polynomial ring onto a finitely presented algebra is finitely generated
author: The Stacks Project Authors
source_version: Stacks Project git a04446e57ec1 (2026-07-28); file algebra.tex; corpus local snapshot 20261012
difficulty_reason: For a ring map R to S of finite presentation, the lemma states that the kernel of any surjection from a polynomial ring onto S is a finitely generated ideal (statement lines 782-787). The proof does not proceed by choosing a minimal presentation or by an induction on the number of variables: it writes down one presentation of S, lifts the given variables into that polynomial ring, combines both sets of variables into one presentation, and describes the kernel of the given surjection as the image of a finitely generated ideal under an explicit comparison map (proof lines 789-798). The construction of that comparison map and the identification of the kernel with the transported ideal is the substance, and the author writes it out. H2.
